author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Bus riders and transportation advocates are pressing Rhode Island officials to keep RIPTA’s main Providence hub at Kennedy Plaza.

The Kennedy Plaza Resilience Coalition scheduled a Tuesday evening rally to oppose proposals that would move the terminal closer to the Amtrak station. Similar relocation ideas have circulated for years as state and city leaders consider changes to downtown transportation.

The coalition argues that moving the hub would spend public money while making downtown access harder for seniors and riders with disabilities. Supporters of a relocation have described potential connections among bus, rail and development projects, but the cited report did not identify a newly approved site or final construction plan.

The dispute remains a planning debate rather than a completed move. Any relocation would require public decisions on design, funding, accessibility and service patterns. Kennedy Plaza currently functions as a central transfer point, so riders are focused on whether a new location would preserve practical connections to jobs, services and other bus routes.
dek: A Providence coalition organized a rally opposing proposals to move the downtown bus terminal near the Amtrak station.
headline: Riders press to keep RIPTA hub at Kennedy Plaza
